question: In a study, adults spent $40 on either a time-saving purchase or a material one. Which lifted their mood more?
answer: The time-saving purchase. In Whillans and colleagues' field experiment, spending $40 on saving time left people less pressed and in a better mood than spending it on a thing. In a survey of about 6,000 people in four countries, those who paid to save time reported more life satisfaction.
move: Price a purchase in hours returned, not only in what it holds.
reference: Whillans, Dunn, Smeets, Bekkers and Norton, Buying time promotes happiness, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2017
